# penalties7

Penalties for regularized and Bayesian regression as S7 objects. A
penalty is $`\rho(D\beta; \theta)`$, made of a linear map $`D`$, a
scalar function $`\rho`$ and hyperparameters $`\theta`$. The object
supplies the value with its normalizing constant, the derivatives in the
coefficients and in the hyperparameters (in closed form for every
penalty that ships), the mixed block, the points where the penalty is
not smooth, the proximal operator where one exists, and, for the
quadratic branches, the rank, the null basis and the log
pseudo-determinant that a marginal criterion uses.

Part of the [statmodels7](https://statmodels7.github.io) toolkit.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("statmodels7/penalties7")
```

## The branches

[`quadratic_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/quadratic_penalty.md)
carries a fixed positive semidefinite matrix $`P`$, an optional map
$`D`$ and one smoothing parameter $`\lambda`$. Its value is the negative
log-density of the Gaussian prior on $`\beta`$ with precision
$`\lambda D^\top P D`$, which is improper when that matrix is singular,
as it is for the second-difference penalty below. The rank, the null
basis and the log pseudo-determinant are computed from the
eigendecomposition of $`D^\top P D`$ when the object is built.

``` r

P <- crossprod(diff(diag(6), differences = 2))   # a second-difference penalty
pen <- quadratic_penalty(P)
c(rank = penalty_rank(pen), nullity = ncol(penalty_null_basis(pen)))
#>    rank nullity 
#>       4       2
penalty_value(pen, rep(1, 6), list(lambda = 1))
#> [1] 1.348774
```

The `blocks` argument builds the penalty of $`I_m \otimes P`$, which is
the penalty of a smooth repeated over the levels of a factor, from the
single block $`P`$. The eigenvalues of the Kronecker product are those
of $`P`$ repeated $`m`$ times, so the rank, the log pseudo-determinant
and the null basis follow from the small matrix. The large matrix is
stored as a sparse matrix and is never decomposed.

``` r

blocked <- quadratic_penalty(P, blocks = 50)
c(rank = penalty_rank(blocked), columns = 6 * 50)
#>    rank columns 
#>     200     300
```

[`additive_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/additive_penalty.md)
is a sum of quadratic penalties with a smoothing parameter on each,
$`S(\lambda) = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k`$, which is the penalty of an
anisotropic tensor-product smooth. The null space of a sum of positive
semidefinite matrices is the intersection of their null spaces and does
not depend on the smoothing parameters, so the rank is computed once, at
construction, from the sum of the components with each one divided by
its largest absolute entry. A count of the nonzero eigenvalues of
$`S(\lambda)`$ itself would fall as the smoothing parameters spread
apart.

``` r

P1 <- crossprod(diff(diag(6), differences = 2))
P2 <- crossprod(diff(diag(6), differences = 1))
add <- additive_penalty(list(P1, P2))
penalty_rank(add)
#> [1] 5
```

[`distrib_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/distrib_penalty.md)
builds a penalty from a continuous
[distributions7](https://statmodels7.github.io/distributions7/) family.
The value is the negative log-density of the family at the coordinates
of $`D\beta`$, taken one coordinate at a time for a univariate family,
which gives a separable penalty, and one block at a time for a
multivariate family.
[`lasso_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ridge_penalty.md)
is a Laplace at zero,
[`elasticnet_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ridge_penalty.md)
the product of a Laplace and a Gaussian, and
[`heavy_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ridge_penalty.md)
a Student t, whose degrees of freedom can be estimated because the
normalizing constant is part of the value.

``` r

lasso <- lasso_penalty(n_coef = 3)

penalty_value(lasso, c(1, -2, 0.5), list(lambda = 2))
#> [1] 7
penalty_kinks(lasso, list(lambda = 2))   # where the density is not smooth
#> [1] 0
```

[`ridge_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ridge_penalty.md)
is the Gaussian at zero written by its precision $`\lambda`$, which is
the quadratic penalty at the identity matrix. It is therefore built by
[`quadratic_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/quadratic_penalty.md)
and not by
[`distrib_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/distrib_penalty.md),
and its hyperparameter is the `lambda` of the quadratic branch. The
separable Gaussian is the same prior written by its standard deviation
$`\sigma = 1/\sqrt{\lambda}`$, and the two values agree to rounding
error. In the ridge, the lasso, the elastic net, SCAD and MCP a larger
`lambda` shrinks harder; in
[`heavy_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ridge_penalty.md)
the hyperparameter `sigma` is a scale, and a larger value shrinks less.

``` r

ridge <- ridge_penalty(n_coef = 3)
penalty_value(ridge, c(1, -1, 2), list(lambda = 1))
#> [1] 5.756816

# the same prior on the separable branch, written by sigma = 1 / sqrt(lambda)
twin <- distrib_penalty(
  distributions7::fixed(distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), mu = 0),
  n_coef = 3)
penalty_value(twin, c(1, -1, 2), list(sigma = 1))
#> [1] 5.756816
```

[`structured_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/structured_penalty.md)
reads a [parameters7](https://statmodels7.github.io/parameters7/) matrix
parameter as the precision of a Gaussian prior, so the hyperparameters
are the free values of that structure and every derivative comes from
its derivative arrays. A structure meant as a covariance is passed as
[`parameters7::inverse_of()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/parameters7/reference/inverse_of.html)
of the structure, which gives a different prior at the same free values.
At a zero log-Cholesky free vector the precision is the identity matrix,
and the penalty equals the ridge at $`\lambda = 1`$.

``` r

st <- structured_penalty(parameters7::log_cholesky(3))
st@params
#> [1] "log_L1" "log_L2" "log_L3" "L2.1"   "L3.1"   "L3.2"
eta <- as.list(stats::setNames(rep(0, length(st@params)), st@params))

c(structured = penalty_value(st, c(1, -1, 2), eta),
  ridge      = penalty_value(ridge, c(1, -1, 2), list(lambda = 1)))
#> structured      ridge 
#>   5.756816   5.756816
```

[`scad_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/scad_penalty.md)
and
[`mcp_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/scad_penalty.md)
are defined by their derivative rather than by a density. Both have the
slope $`\lambda`$ of the lasso at the origin and become flat far from
it, so a large coefficient is not shrunk at all, while the lasso shrinks
every nonzero coefficient by the same amount. The second hyperparameter
(`a` for SCAD, `gamma` for MCP) sets the point $`a\lambda`$ or
$`\gamma\lambda`$ beyond which the penalty is flat. Their value is
bounded, so $`\exp(-\rho)`$ is not integrable and they carry no
normalizing constant.
[`is_proper()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/is_proper.md)
returns `TRUE` for the penalties that are proper priors.

``` r

scad <- scad_penalty(n_coef = 3)
mcp  <- mcp_penalty(n_coef = 3)

vapply(list(ridge = ridge, lasso = lasso, scad = scad, mcp = mcp),
       is_proper, logical(1))
#> ridge lasso  scad   mcp 
#>  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE

# the derivative: close to lambda near zero, zero past the threshold
b <- c(0.2, 2, 8)
rbind(lasso = penalty_gradient(lasso, b, list(lambda = 1)),
      scad  = penalty_gradient(scad,  b, list(lambda = 1, a = 3.7)),
      mcp   = penalty_gradient(mcp,   b, list(lambda = 1, gamma = 3)))
#>            [,1]      [,2] [,3]
#> lasso 1.0000000 1.0000000    1
#> scad  1.0000000 0.6296296    0
#> mcp   0.9333333 0.3333333    0
```

## The proximal operator

[`penalty_prox()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_prox.md)
evaluates
$`\operatorname{prox}_{t\rho}(v) = \arg\min_\beta \{\tfrac{1}{2}\lVert\beta -
v\rVert^2 + t\,\rho(\beta;\theta)\}`$, the operator that a proximal
gradient method applies after each gradient step. For the quadratic and
structured branches it is a linear solve, under any map. For the
Gaussian, Laplace and elastic-net priors at zero it has a closed form,
and for SCAD and MCP it is the closed piecewise operator, available
while the step keeps the problem convex (a step below $`a - 1`$ for SCAD
and below $`\gamma`$ for MCP). For any other separable parent with a
smooth log-density it is the global minimizer among the roots of the
stationary condition, coordinate by coordinate. The separable operators
need the identity map or a diagonal one.
[`has_prox()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/has_prox.md)
returns `FALSE` for the additive branch, for a separable penalty under a
map that is not diagonal and for a multivariate parent, which have no
operator.

``` r

v <- c(2, -0.4, 0.9)
penalty_prox(lasso, v, step = 1, theta = list(lambda = 1))   # soft threshold
#> [1] 1 0 0
sign(v) * pmax(abs(v) - 1, 0)                                # by hand
#> [1] 1 0 0
```

## Validation

[`check_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/check_penalty.md)
compares the derivatives of a penalty with numerical references computed
by numDeriv: the gradient and the Hessian in the coefficients, the
gradient and every entry of the Hessian in the hyperparameters, and the
mixed block. For a quadratic penalty it also checks the three-point
identity of a quadratic form, the log pseudo-determinant, the rank and
the null basis. It does not test the proximal operator. The function is
meant above all for a penalty written outside the package; the article
[Defining a
penalty](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/articles/defining-a-penalty.html)
writes one and validates it, and the examples of
[`check_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/check_penalty.md)
show the row that fails when a gradient is wrong.

``` r

res <- check_penalty(ridge_penalty(n_coef = 3), verbose = FALSE)
all(res$status == "OK")
#> [1] TRUE
```

# Package index

## The class and the generics

The base class and the generics of every penalty: the value with its
normalizing constant, the derivatives in the coefficients and in the
hyperparameters, the mixed block, the points where the penalty is not
smooth, and the predicates and quantities that a fitting layer reads.

- [`penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty.md)
  : S7 Base Class for Penalties
- [`penalty_value()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_value.md)
  : Value of a Penalty
- [`penalty_gradient()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_gradient.md)
  [`penalty_hessian()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_gradient.md)
  : Coefficient Derivatives of a Penalty
- [`penalty_grad_theta()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_grad_theta.md)
  [`penalty_hess_theta()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_grad_theta.md)
  [`penalty_cross()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_grad_theta.md)
  : Hyperparameter Derivatives of a Penalty
- [`penalty_kinks()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_kinks.md)
  : Points Where a Penalty Is Not Smooth
- [`penalty_readable()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_readable.md)
  : Interpretable Quantities of a Penalty's Hyperparameters
- [`penalty_draw()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_draw.md)
  : Drawing From a Penalty Read as a Prior
- [`is_proper()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/is_proper.md)
  : Is a Penalty a Proper Prior?
- [`is_quadratic()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/is_quadratic.md)
  : Is a Penalty a Quadratic Form?
- [`penalty_matrix()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_matrix.md)
  [`penalty_rank()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_matrix.md)
  [`penalty_null_basis()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_matrix.md)
  [`penalty_logpdet()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_matrix.md)
  : Quantities of a Quadratic Penalty for a Marginal Criterion

## Derivatives for a marginal criterion

A Laplace approximation to a marginal likelihood differentiates the
determinant of the penalized information, so it needs the hyperparameter
derivatives of the coefficient Hessian and of the mixed block. The
hyperparameters of a penalty that supplies them can be estimated by REML
or ML. SCAD, MCP and a separable penalty with a kink do not supply them.

- [`penalty_dhessian()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_dhessian.md)
  : The Derivative of the Coefficient Hessian in the Hyperparameters
- [`penalty_d2hessian()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_d2hessian.md)
  : The Second Derivative of the Coefficient Hessian in the
  Hyperparameters
- [`penalty_dcross()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_dcross.md)
  : The Derivative of the Mixed Block in the Hyperparameters
- [`penalty_dhessian_beta()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_dhessian_beta.md)
  : The Derivative of the Coefficient Hessian in the Coefficients
- [`penalty_d2hessian_beta()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_d2hessian_beta.md)
  [`penalty_dhessian_beta_theta()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_d2hessian_beta.md)
  : Second Derivatives of the Coefficient Hessian in the Coefficients
  and the Hyperparameters
- [`beta_quadratic()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/beta_quadratic.md)
  : Is a Penalty Quadratic in the Coefficients?

## The quadratic branch

A fixed matrix P, an optional map D and one smoothing parameter lambda,
so the penalty is the negative log-density of a Gaussian prior with
precision lambda D’PD, improper when D’PD is singular. The rank, the
null basis and the log pseudo-determinant are computed from D’PD when
the object is built.

- [`quadratic_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/quadratic_penalty.md)
  : Construct a Quadratic Penalty
- [`QuadraticPenalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/QuadraticPenalty.md)
  : S7 Class for the Quadratic Penalty

## The additive branch

A sum of quadratic penalties with a smoothing parameter on each, which
is the penalty of an anisotropic tensor-product smooth. The rank is
computed at construction from the sum of the components, each divided by
its largest absolute entry, because the null space of the sum does not
depend on the smoothing parameters.

- [`additive_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/additive_penalty.md)
  : Construct a Sum of Quadratic Penalties
- [`AdditivePenalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/AdditivePenalty.md)
  : S7 Class for a Sum of Quadratic Penalties

## The separable branch

The negative log-density of a continuous distributions7 family at the
coordinates of the mapped coefficients, one coordinate at a time for a
univariate family and one block at a time for a multivariate one. The
lasso is a Laplace at zero, the elastic net the product of a Laplace and
a Gaussian, and the heavy-tailed prior a Student t. The ridge,
documented with them, is the Gaussian at zero written by its precision
and is built on the quadratic branch.

- [`distrib_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/distrib_penalty.md)
  : Construct a Separable Penalty From a Distribution
- [`distrib_kinks()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/distrib_kinks.md)
  : Where the Parent's Log-Density Has a Kink
- [`ridge_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ridge_penalty.md)
  [`lasso_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ridge_penalty.md)
  [`elasticnet_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ridge_penalty.md)
  [`heavy_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ridge_penalty.md)
  : The Named Penalties
- [`DistribPenalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/DistribPenalty.md)
  : S7 Class for the Separable Penalty

## The structured branch

A parameters7 matrix parameter used as the precision, so the
hyperparameters are the free values of that structure and every
derivative comes from its derivative arrays.

- [`structured_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/structured_penalty.md)
  : Construct a Structured Quadratic Penalty
- [`StructuredPenalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/StructuredPenalty.md)
  : S7 Class for the Structured Quadratic Penalty

## SCAD and MCP

Defined by their derivative rather than by a density. Their value is
bounded, so exp(-value) is not integrable: they are improper, carry no
normalizing constant and cannot come from a distribution.

- [`scad_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/scad_penalty.md)
  [`mcp_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/scad_penalty.md)
  : Construct the SCAD and MCP Penalties
- [`ScadPenalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ScadPenalty.md)
  [`McpPenalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/ScadPenalty.md)
  : S7 Classes for the SCAD and MCP Penalties

## The proximal operator

The operator that a proximal gradient method applies after each gradient
step: a linear solve for the quadratic and structured branches, a closed
form for the Gaussian, Laplace, elastic-net, SCAD and MCP penalties, and
a coordinatewise root for any other separable parent with a smooth
log-density.

- [`penalty_prox()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_prox.md)
  : Proximal Operator of a Penalty
- [`penalty_prox_spec()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/penalty_prox_spec.md)
  : The Proximal Operator as a Piecewise Linear Table
- [`prox_apply()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/prox_apply.md)
  : Apply a Piecewise Linear Table
- [`has_prox()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/has_prox.md)
  : Does a Penalty Supply a Proximal Operator?

## Validation

Numerical checks of the derivatives of a penalty, meant above all for a
penalty written outside the package.

- [`check_penalty()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/reference/check_penalty.md)
  : Check a Penalty Numerically
